item.title: CKB Talk Daily Brief - 2026-11-12

item.title: Spark Program | zk-Lock for CKB (2 posts)
item.description: Hi @xingtianchunyan and the committee, Thank you for your patience. The interactive frontend asked for in post #22 is live: https://zk-lock.vercel.app/ It takes about a minute, with no wallet and nothing to install. You type a secret word, your browser produces the proof, and that proof spends a real cell on Pudge. It uses the project’s own SDK and deployed contracts rather than being a separate mock, and a CKB node runs the deployed script against each proof so the verdict shown is the chain’s own. There is also a plain-English explainer with no code in it, covering what zk-Lock enables, what each use case gets you, and what is not true of it yet: zk-Lock/docs/explainer.md at main ·...

item.title: Ckbup: one installer for CKB command-line tools (early progress, feedback welcome) (1 posts)
item.description: I’ve started building ckbup, a small open-source installer and version manager for CKB’s command-line tools, in the spirit of rustup. It’s free and I’m not asking for anything; I’m sharing it early to get feedback from people who actually set up CKB machines. Why Getting the CKB tools onto a machine still means a different route for each one: there’s no package-manager install for ckb-cli, only “manually downloading a .zip/.tar.gz from the Releases page” (ckb-cli#685); some tools ship no arm64 builds, so ARM users build from source, which “works but takes 20-30 min” (ckb-light-client#272, fiber#1186); cargo install ckb-cli fails on Windows (ckb-cli#660). item.description: [Status Update] M1: dashboards and discovery are live M1 is done and live on testnet at crowdcell.vercel.app. What shipped: Wallet-aware indexer endpoints, so the app knows which campaigns and pledges belong to the connected wallet. “My campaigns” (crowdcell.vercel.app/dashboard/campaigns): each campaign’s status, amount raised, backers, and the actions available right now. “My pledges” (crowdcell.vercel.app/dashboard/pledges): each pledge’s status and outcome, plus receipts and deposits you can reclaim. item.title: Spark Program | CellGuard × CrowdCell — Real Transaction Policy Integration Pilot (1 posts)
item.description: Hey Dang, nice to see this, and happy to review the pledge profile once you’ve pinned it. A few things that should save you time. The live deployment is the one in deployment/deployed-contracts-testnet.json (redeployed Oct 31), that’s what crowdcell.vercel.app runs. The fallback hashes in off-chain/indexer/src/index.ts are still the old ones, I’ll fix that, so don’t take them from there. Also the pledge tx the app sends isn’t TransactionBuilder.createPledge, it’s built in off-chain/frontend/src/app/campaigns/[id]/page.tsx: the campaign cell goes in, then campaign + pledge + receipt come out, with the campaign capacity and scripts unchanged and total pledged bumped by the pledge amount....

item.title: iCKB Contracts Revisited: Old Code, New Audit (1 posts)
item.description: Last time I asked if the contracts accept something they shouldn’t. This time I asked what all those tests never even touched: which parts of the code on chain had never run? So I traced it, instruction by instruction. About a third of each contract had never run. Most of that can’t run at all, but a few corners can. Each one now has its own test. Same result: nothing new found!! Every reachable corner tested: the corners a transaction can reach now run in the tests. A close reading of the rest found nothing else that could change a result. The tools that built them too: every library compiled into the contracts got checked from its code. So did about 2,200 known bugs of the compiler that...
